While meeting with President Obama at the White House, the Prime Minister raised issues surrounding extradition arrangements. Critics claim the existing treaty is biased towards the US, as they need to provide less evidence when requesting the extradition of UK citizens. Nevertheless, a senior judge reviewing the treaty in 2011 considered it fair to Britons. BBC's Nick Robinson reported that Mr. Cameron discussed the real-world effects of these rules during the two-hour meeting on Wednesday. The Prime Minister's US visit is a three-day official trip. The 2003 US-UK extradition treaty has been controversial, particularly due to high-profile cases involving British citizens such as Christopher Tappin and Gary McKinnon. Bodies like the Joint Committee on Human Rights in Parliament have urged the government to renegotiate the treaty, citing its perceived unfairness.

In Fiscal Kombat, players assume the role of Mr. Melenchon, traversing urban landscapes to battle oligarchs and political adversaries. The objective is to seize wealth from the wealthy elite to finance Melenchon's political platform. Players are challenged to accumulate maximum funds while evading deadly assaults from affluent figures. Melenchon faces off against a roster of "boss" characters, such as former President Nicolas Sarkozy, IMF head Christine Lagarde, tax cheat Jerome Cahuzac, and L'Oreal magnate Liliane Bettencourt. He is also tasked with overcoming presidential contenders Emmanuel Macron and Francois Fillon from the 2017 French election. According to Le Monde, the game was conceived by Melenchon's backers on the Jeuxvideo.com forum and has since garnered the candidate's complete endorsement.

The potential merger of Bouygues Telecom and Vivendi's SFR is designed to create France's number one mobile operator, shrinking the national market to three major players. Altice, Numericable's parent company, has also made an offer for SFR, the financial details of which are not public. If approved, the union of Bouygues Telecom and SFR, currently France's second and third largest mobile providers respectively, would eclipse Orange in market share. The merger hinges on regulatory approval from French and EU competition watchdogs, particularly considering analogous issues surrounding Telefonica's attempt to acquire E-Plus in Germany. Analysts view the Bouygues proposal as part of a broader consolidation movement within the mobile sector.

Doreen Collyer, a 60-year-old former University of Chester lecturer, tragically lost her life in a shark attack during a scuba diving excursion in Perth on Sunday. Authorities suspect a 16-foot great white shark was the culprit, as reported by the Australian Broadcasting Corporation (ABC). Her husband, David Collyer, remembered her as a "beautiful person" and his "loving wife." The couple had moved to Australia from Neston, Cheshire, about five years ago. Mrs. Collyer held an advanced open water diving certification. ABC stated that although her diving partner managed to bring her ashore, she died from her injuries at the scene. Prof Annette McIntosh-Scott from the University of Chester expressed deep sorrow over the loss of Mrs. Collyer, calling her a "hugely valued and loved member of staff" who dedicated 15 years to the Faculty of Health and Social Care, emphasizing her lasting legacy of commitment to teaching, child healthcare, and her students' well-being.

The American warbler, potentially transported by Hurricane Gert during its South American migration, has been identified in England, a first according to Portland Bird Observatory's Martin Cade, who described the sighting as "pretty amazing." Typically found in the United States, these birds annually migrate between North and South America. Cade theorizes the warbler was swept across the Atlantic from the Caribbean by storm winds, mirroring a recent warbler sighting at Mizen Head in southwest Ireland. The robin-sized bird, "active and feeding well," may be preparing to migrate south towards Spain and Africa, Cade suggests. News of the rare sighting on Monday drew birdwatchers from far-flung areas, including the Midlands, South Wales, and Yorkshire.

Despite Alexis Sanchez having only a year remaining on his contract, Arsene Wenger is confident the 28-year-old Chilean forward, instrumental in Arsenal's FA Cup semi-final win against Manchester City, will stay with the Gunners and agree to a new deal. The Arsenal manager also affirmed he would not sell Sanchez to a rival Premier League club. Even with Wenger's own future at the north London club undecided – his contract ends this season and a two-year extension is proposed – the 67-year-old maintains he is already working on identifying key transfer targets for the next season, underscoring their significance to the club's long-term prospects.

Following the escape of convicted murderers Richard Matt and David Sweat from Clinton Correctional Facility using power tools, Gene Palmer is the second prison employee to be arrested, after Joyce Mitchell who is already facing charges for aiding the breakout. Palmer was arraigned and released on bail, charged with offenses such as promoting prison contraband, evidence tampering, and official misconduct. His lawyer, Andrew Brockway, admitted Palmer delivered the meat but asserted his client didn't know it concealed tools or that the inmates were plotting an escape, adding that Palmer regrets his actions and plans to plead not guilty. The H3 project, designed to consolidate administrative operations for police, fire, and council services in Hampshire and Oxfordshire, targeted £5 million in yearly savings. Since its launch in 2014, the Police Federation has documented numerous errors, including payroll problems. Hampshire's PCC expects improvements by May, citing continued investment. A report for PCC Michael Lane revealed that H3 has led to recruitment challenges, complicated employee sick leave procedures, and increased officers' administrative workload, reducing their effectiveness. In February 2016, 1,300 officers received incorrect pay, with flawed allowance calculations in March. Additionally, a 2015 BBC investigation found that payment delays to Hampshire County Council suppliers had tripled under the new system. Two men, a 22-year-old from Sleaford and a 25-year-old from Bracknell, were arrested on Thursday for their suspected involvement in repeated attempts to infiltrate Microsoft's network between January and March. The arrests, made under the UK's Computer Misuse Act which criminalizes unauthorized computer access, followed allegations that the pair were part of a larger group plotting a cyberattack on Microsoft to steal customer data. The South East Regional Organised Crime Unit (Serocu) conducted the raids, seizing devices believed to be connected to the alleged offenses, as stated by Det Sgt Rob Bryant.

Ariya Jutanugarn, at 20 years old, delivered a perfect round of six birdies, putting her in contention to surpass the tournament's record of 19-under par. South Korea's Mirim Lee, who previously led, slipped to second place following a round of 69. Catriona Matthew from Scotland trails in fourth, six shots back. Jutanugarn hopes to become the first Thai golfer to secure a major championship victory, drawing on lessons from her ANA Inspiration experience where she struggled in the final stretch. Showing remarkable composure in her third round, Jutanugarn shared with BBC Sport that she now comprehends how to handle pressure and is concentrating on the aspects within her control.

At an IMF gathering in Washington, Christine Lagarde affirmed the success of the UK's economic approach. She minimized differences between the IMF's deficit forecasts and the more optimistic projections from the Office for Budget Responsibility, attributing them to differing methodologies while asserting their fundamental equivalence. Lagarde, appearing alongside George Osborne and Wolfgang Schaeuble, pointed out the typical conservatism of deficit forecasts in election years, reflecting uncertainty about the full implementation of stated policies. She also recognized the UK's achievement in combining spending reductions with revenue enhancements, and highlighted the UK's relatively strong growth performance in comparison to other European countries.

In response to the rapid growth and technological advancements in the private hire industry, Transport for London (TfL) is weighing new rules for these companies. The proposed regulations include mandatory English and map-reading assessments, a requirement for a permanent office phone line, and the option for customers to schedule rides up to a week ahead. Uber has voiced opposition, arguing the changes would drastically change its service model. Black cab drivers, who recently protested outside City Hall, have been pushing for more stringent rules. Uber's app, which uses GPS to connect riders with drivers, provide fare estimates, and facilitate cashless payments, offers a lower-cost alternative to traditional taxis. While TfL asserts the consultation seeks to raise industry standards, Uber contends it is being unfairly targeted and that the proposed rules would result in higher costs for consumers and increased traffic.

Music festival "superfans," predominantly male, are a powerful economic force, spending an average of £581 each year, often opting for VIP experiences or upgraded camping options. These dedicated fans also buck the trend by purchasing music in physical or downloaded formats more often than average consumers. A survey of 504 UK festival attendees, commissioned by Eventbrite, reveals that these "superfans" wield considerable influence, shaping the festival landscape through their recommendations. Although they comprise 28% of the festival-going population, and a majority (54%) are happy to attend festivals alone, their loyalty is not guaranteed; almost half (46%) believe festivals are becoming overly commercialized. In the UK, the music festival scene is vibrant, with over 100 events annually, from major gatherings like Glastonbury and T In The Park to more intimate affairs.

The pound sterling surged, appreciating by 1.86% against the dollar to $1.32.40 and 1.73% versus the euro to €1.19.57. The FTSE 100 briefly hit an 11-month high before falling back to close virtually flat at 6,680.69, a slight dip of 2.17 points or 0.03%. Meanwhile, the FTSE 250, focused on UK companies, advanced by 68.75 points, or 0.4%, to 16,775.14. The property market, which had suffered post-Brexit losses, was boosted by Galliford Try's statement projecting full-year profits in line with forecasts, leading to an 8.5% jump in its share price. Financial stocks, also impacted by the referendum, recovered somewhat, with Aviva shares rising 4.26% and Lloyds Banking Group also showing positive results.

Last April, a submarine snagged the nets of a fishing boat, pulling it 18 miles from the County Down shoreline and causing significant damage. The skipper noted the crew's good fortune to be unharmed, though repairs were estimated at approximately £10,000. The Ministry of Defence (MoD) has now admitted a British submarine's involvement, abandoning its usual practice of silence regarding submarine activities. The Royal Navy explained that "new information" confirmed a UK submarine was responsible for the damage to the MV Karen. Minister for the Armed Forces Penny Mordaunt issued a formal statement to Parliament, conveying sincere regret for "the incident, the delay in identifying and addressing the events on that day, and their consequences," citing the submarine's failure to correctly recognize the Karen as a fishing boat with deployed nets as the cause.

Kian Delos Santos was killed by police officers who claimed he was a drug dealer who fought back during his arrest. However, CCTV footage appeared to show plainclothes officers forcibly taking the 17-year-old. Evidence suggests he was on his knees when he was shot. Hundreds attended his Manila funeral, with some protesting President Duterte's aggressive anti-drug campaign, which has been popular among Filipinos concerned about drug-related crime. Reuters reported that nuns, priests, and hundreds of children chanting "justice for Kian, justice for all" marched from a church to the cemetery for his burial. At the Mass, his father, Saldy, briefly spoke, declaring his son's innocence and condemning the police, asking emotionally, "Don't they have a heart?" and urging them to attend church.

Constructed in less than a year, the new 72-kilometer (44-mile) channel, running alongside a portion of the existing canal, facilitates two-way navigation and accommodates larger vessels. On Saturday, a convoy of international container ships, escorted by helicopters and naval vessels, successfully completed a test transit of the waterway. The Sinai Peninsula, bordering the canal, has been plagued by Islamic insurgents who have caused hundreds of fatalities since President Mohammed Morsi's removal in 2013. The original Suez Canal, linking the Mediterranean and Red Seas, opened nearly 150 years ago. Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi anticipates that the expanded canal, which presently handles 7% of global maritime commerce, will boost economic activity and generate employment opportunities throughout the country.

James Carragher, previously convicted of sex offenses in 1993 and 2004, receiving sentences of seven and fourteen years respectively, is now standing trial at Leeds Crown Court, facing 50 charges of indecent assault. The alleged crimes took place between the 1970s and 1990s at St William's in Market Weighton, East Riding of Yorkshire. This now-defunct Catholic-run home for boys with behavioral problems, managed by the De La Salle order, also saw two other ex-employees face trial. Carragher, who was in charge of St. William's from 1976 to 1990, along with the other two, are accused of abusing 19 former students. According to Prosecutor Richard Wright QC, Carragher possessed a "dedicated sexual attraction to children, particularly young boys," which he masked "under a facade of respectability."

Cardoso, aged 23, finalized a three-year contract after his transfer from Vitoria Setubal for an undisclosed fee. In an interview with Rangers TV, he conveyed his eagerness to adapt to the new environment and way of life, expressing optimism about his prospects and pledging to help the team win, acknowledging the high standards expected at a club like Rangers. Cardoso, who previously played for Portugal's Under-21 team and made 23 appearances for Vitoria Setubal last season after his move from Benfica, joins Bruno Alves, who came from Cagliari, as the second Portuguese center-back to sign with Rangers this summer. Additionally, midfielder Dalcio has joined Ibrox on a loan agreement from Benfica.

Veteran Mugabe critic Morgan Tsvangirai and former Vice-President Joice Mujuru have declared they will work together in the next election, although their presidential candidate is still to be determined. The 93-year-old President Mugabe, who has governed Zimbabwe since its independence in 1980, plans to seek re-election. Tsvangirai hailed the collaboration as "the foundation for creating a wide-ranging alliance to challenge Zanu-PF" in the lead-up to the election. This alliance is a key step in uniting a divided opposition and, should it succeed, would be the strongest unified opposition Mugabe has encountered since taking office in 1980.

In a Wednesday meeting with Members of the European Parliament, Jean-Claude Juncker voiced his backing for "democratic expressions" and promised to honor Scotland's choice. Asked by Catalan MEP Josep Maria Terricabras about the EU membership prospects of Catalonia and Scotland, Juncker said a letter requesting membership wasn't enough. Later, when Scottish UKIP MEP David Coburn questioned the EU status of an independent Scotland, Juncker explained that the final decision lies with the UK.

According to a report, incoming Harvard students shared deeply offensive material in a private Facebook chat, including jokes about child abuse, sexual assault, pedophilia, the Holocaust, and racist insults. Harvard's reaction, described as "draconian" by free speech proponents, was covered by the Crimson, the university's student newspaper. This chat group, a spin-off from a larger messaging group for the incoming class, was created for sharing memes and more mature content. To gain access to this sub-group, prospective students were required to make and share a "provocative" meme. Once the group was discovered, Harvard administrators launched an investigation and interviewed students involved.

After the controversial sentencing of Brock Turner, the former Stanford swimmer, in June 2016, community leaders in Santa Clara County began a formal signature-gathering process on Monday to potentially recall Judge Aaron Persky next year. Persky sentenced Turner, who was convicted of sexual assault in January 2015 and faced a maximum 14-year sentence, to just six months in jail, and he was released after only three months. The recall petition notice states that Persky's lenient sentence for Turner's sexual assault of an unconscious woman ignited international condemnation. Michele Dauber, a Stanford law professor leading the recall effort with 50 other community leaders, announced at a press conference that residents of Santa Clara County deserve a judge who values victim protection over the rights of rapists, and stressed women's commitment to fighting rape culture with concrete action.

Each year, contestants in the annual contest have five minutes to deliver the most convincing and imaginative tall tale they can create. This year's winner, George Kemp of Maryport, Cumbria, was taken aback by his victory, admitting he was battling a chest infection. His winning narrative centered on "meeting Donald Trump and his wife at an underwater hotel." He elaborated, "The story involved building a small submarine out of my father's old bubble car." He added, "We traveled to the Isle of Man in the bubble car and met various celebrities aboard a Scottish submarine made of shortbread tins. Subsequently, Nicola Sturgeon and Alex Salmond sold some of these massive shortbread tin submarines to the United States." Mike Naylor, also known as Monkey Liar, from Wasdale, the previous year's champion, took second place, with Helen Jordan coming in third. Previous victors include the comedian and television star Sue Perkins.

The inquiry found that just over a quarter (28%) of Welsh speakers had used the language with their GPs, dentists, or opticians. Ms. Huws voiced her expectation that the report would be a catalyst for change, guaranteeing patient-centered healthcare. Government ministers responded positively to the report, promising a response in half a year. Based on the experiences of more than a thousand Welsh speakers, the investigation emphasized that 90% felt they should have the right to communicate in Welsh with the NHS, irrespective of where they lived in Wales. Furthermore, Welsh speakers reported feeling uneasy and finding it difficult to express themselves to doctors who did not speak Welsh. The report puts forward 33 recommendations to the Welsh government, pressing ministers to deliver explicit policy guidance, an implementation strategy, and a schedule for transforming primary care services.

The proposed legislation aims to revoke sections of the UK's 2016 Trade Union Act, potentially modifying current restrictions on industrial action in the NHS, fire service, schools, and other Welsh devolved services. Although UK ministers argue that industrial relations are a Westminster matter, a key aspect of the UK law stipulates that strikes need the backing of 40% of a union's members via ballot. The Welsh Assembly's Equality, Local Government and Communities Committee agreed that the new law is vital to preserve Wales' collaborative "social-partnership" approach. Welsh Finance Secretary Mark Drakeford stated in March that it would be a "democratic outrage" if London tried to block the Welsh Trade Union Bill. The Labour Welsh Government argues that UK ministers should not limit union activities in devolved Welsh services, such as healthcare and education. Conservative AM Janet Finch-Saunders opposed the committee report, meaning it lacked unanimous support.

After the tragic death of Evha Jannath, an 11-year-old who fell from a boat on the Splash Canyon ride at Drayton Manor during a school trip on Tuesday, several theme parks have responded. Drayton Manor will remain closed on Friday for safety checks. As a precautionary measure, Merlin Entertainments, which runs Alton Towers and Legoland Windsor, has temporarily shut down comparable water rides, with plans to reopen them on Friday. Conversely, Lightwater Valley and West Midland Safari Park have decided to keep their water rides open following the incident.

Rangers secured the trophy after three previous failed attempts, thanks to Ally Gilchrist's own goal and a strong strike from James Tavernier, which put them in a dominant position. Andy Halliday's penalty and Kenny Miller's goal from close range cemented Rangers' win. Mark Warburton's team will now play against Celtic in the Scottish Cup semi-final next Sunday. Having lost Challenge Cup matches to Queen of the South, Raith Rovers, and Alloa Athletic in the past, Rangers finally won the title and are now preparing to face the Premiership leaders at Hampden, where a new pitch will be installed before the game due to the poor state of the current one. The existing pitch, which cost £200,000 and was laid just five weeks ago, will be replaced because it has not settled properly, and this was deemed not safe for the final match between Rangers and League One's Peterhead, who were heavy underdogs at 22-1.

The Royal College of Midwives (RCM) is facing unprecedented action as its members have voted decisively, with a 90% majority, for a four-hour strike – the first in the organization's 134-year history. The Department of Health has responded with disappointment, promising to work with trusts to ensure the safety of mothers and babies and reaffirming their commitment to dialogue. The RCM is now urgently seeking talks with the health minister to resolve the dispute. According to Bredagh Hughes, RCM NI director, midwives are seeking pay parity with their colleagues in Wales, Scotland, and England, who have already received a 1% pay increase. She clarified that the dispute lies with the Department of Health and employers, not with the women in their care, and guaranteed full emergency cover, ensuring no woman will be at risk, even if striking midwives are required to cover staff shortages.

Tesco Bank clarified that the actual number of current account holders affected by the recent fraudulent activity is under 10,000, a figure significantly lower than the initially estimated 20,000. The bank assured customers that their personal information was not compromised and that all impacted accounts have received full refunds. CEO Benny Higgins characterized the incident as "a systematic, sophisticated attack" that occurred over the weekend, further stating that all affected customers were compensated, and the temporary suspension of online debit transactions was lifted, returning accounts to normal operation. The restriction on online debit card payments for current account users, put in place on Sunday to prevent further criminal activity, has now been removed. Higgins also repeated the bank's apology for the worry and inconvenience caused, emphasizing that they have a firm grasp of the attack's characteristics.

A BBC London/Newsnight investigation revealed widespread fraud within the Construction Skills Certification Scheme (CSCS), the UK's leading certification for builders, which mandates that construction workers possess a card verifying their skills and safety knowledge. Carl Rhymer of the Construction Industry Training Board (CITB) stated that 6,000 cardholders must re-sit the exam. Required by nine of the UK's largest construction companies, Crossrail, and Heathrow, the CSCS card became accessible through corrupt test centers offering guaranteed passes for a fee. This allowed workers with poor English skills to gain qualifications and work on dangerous sites. The BBC investigation highlighted Wep HSE in Ealing, where director Garet Estensen was seen reading answers from a screen and directing candidates. Estensen refused to comment when confronted with the evidence. Future Training was also named as one of the centers involved.

The cyber attackers are requesting a ransom of 100 Bitcoin, which translates to roughly $70,000 (£56,000 ; €66,000). As a countermeasure, staff disabled all network-linked ticket vending machines. Across the city's transit infrastructure, computers, including those within stations, became unusable, displaying a message from the hackers stating "You Hacked, ALL Data Encrypted. Contact For Key(cryptom27@yandex.com)ID:681 ,Enter”. Yandex is a Russian-based firm that offers email and social media platforms. Despite the attack, train services continued without disruption, and a comprehensive inquiry has been initiated by city officials. Speaking to the BBC, a representative confirmed that "There has been no impact to the transit service, to our safety systems or to our customer's personal information,” and also noted that "The incident remains under investigation, so it wouldn't be appropriate to provide any additional details at this point." The city's Municipal Transportation Agency (Muni) manages trains, streetcars, and buses.

In the madison, the last race of the event, the British pair was defeated by Moreno de Pauw and Kenny de Ketele of Belgium. Wiggins, 36, plans to retire after the Ghent Six Day race in November, but hinted he might change his mind. He quipped that "money talks," and added, "After a week like this, who wouldn't want to come back? I don't know. I love racing." The five-time Olympic gold medalist considered the Lee Valley velodrome, where he trained as a youth at the Eastway facility and which hosted the London 2012 track events, an appropriate venue to end his British racing career. He told Eurosport it holds "fantastic memories" and that he will "always come back," probably as a spectator next year. Wiggins and Cavendish started competing in the event last Tuesday.

The Air Accidents Investigation Branch (AAIB) report revealed that cockpit recordings showed the aircraft reacting to the pilot's commands. The report also confirmed that pilot Andy Hill ejected from the plane during the final moments of the crash on August 22nd, though it is unclear whether Hill initiated the ejection. The 51-year-old pilot remains hospitalized in serious but stable condition. The AAIB report further explained that the Hawker Hunter's canopy detached upon initial impact, causing the release and ignition of fuel and fuel vapor. The jet subsequently disintegrated into four parts, ejecting both Hill and his seat. The investigation is ongoing to determine "if the pilot attempted to initiate ejection or if the canopy and pilot's seat were liberated as a result of impact damage to the cockpit."

Around 200 top-tier athletes and up to 25,000 recreational runners are set to participate in a 13.1-mile race on Saturday, March 26th. The race starts close to Cardiff Castle and finishes on King Edward VII Avenue, located in the heart of the city. Dave Bedford, a former world record holder in the 10,000m, lauded the course for its flat terrain and ability to highlight both Cardiff's historical appeal and contemporary progress. Runners will pass notable landmarks including the Millennium Stadium, Cardiff City Stadium, Penarth Marina, Cardiff Bay Barrage, Wales Millennium Centre, and Roath Park Lake, before a grand finale in the city center. This 2016 championship represents the event's debut in Wales. Cardiff, which has hosted a yearly half marathon since 2003, expects that the World Half Marathon will solidify its reputation as a leading racing location.

The area between Bo'ness Harbour and the former Kinneil colliery is set to become a haven for local wildlife and plants, establishing Falkirk Council's second Local Nature Reserve. The council aims to utilize this designation to obtain funding for the area's preservation. This new status represents a transformation for the site, which was an industrial hub for almost 200 years until the main colliery closed in 1983. Parts of the area were already recognized for their ecological importance, with the mudflats and offshore "island" holding a Special Protection Area status due to their conservation value. Councillor Adrian Mahoney, convener of leisure, tourism, and community, welcomed the Kinneil foreshore's new designation, pointing out that this year marks three decades since the closure of Kinneil Colliery, the last local mine.

Despite claiming his affiliation with a social housing firm had no bearing on a 2013 housing development discussion in east Dorset, Spencer Flower was found guilty of unlawful voting because the company stood to benefit from the plan's approval. The 72-year-old Conservative councillor, from Verwood, Dorset, will remain in his public office role despite the conviction. He received a six-month conditional discharge and was ordered to pay Â£930 in costs. A district judge at Bournemouth Magistrates' Court concluded he breached the Localism Act 2011. Leaving the court, Flower, expressing "surprise and disappointment" with the ruling which he called a "technicality," refused to comment on his political future. He emphasized that the conditional discharge was the "lowest possible penalty" and the court recognized there was no evidence of "any personal gain or intent."

In 1964, Cilla Black, who died in 2015, achieved a UK top 10 hit with "It's for You," a track written by John Lennon and Paul McCartney. McCartney had previously recorded the song earlier that year and gifted it to Black during her performance at the London Palladium. The recording, once thought to be lost, was found by Black's nephew. At a Beatles Memorabilia Auction at Liverpool's Unity Theatre, the disc fetched £18,000, with the anonymous purchaser paying a total of £21,060 including commission. Frustrated by the overwhelming number of choices and lengthy pre-recorded messages in call centre menus, Mr. Clarke launched the project. He discovered that some automated systems offer nearly 80 different options, and navigating these menus could take callers over four minutes just to connect with the right service. As an example, Mr. Clarke pointed out that even though reaching an advisor at HM Revenue and Customs only requires four button presses, the entire process can still take six minutes because of the time spent listening to each menu level. In response, HMRC stated that they are actively improving their services. A spokesman said, "HMRC is investigating ways to improve its interactive voice responses and plans to introduce new speech recognition technology." This technology will allow the system to respond to spoken requests instead of requiring button presses. Mr. Clarke noted that HMRC expects to implement these changes later this year.

Despite Syria's apparent failure to meet Sunday's deadline for chemical weapon removal, envoy Sigrid Kaag stressed the necessity of meeting the 30 June target for complete destruction. The Russian-US agreement to eliminate Syria's chemical weapons followed a fatal sarin attack near Damascus the previous year. This international initiative, monitored by the UN Security Council and the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW), seeks to dismantle Syria's chemical weapons program. Although previous deadlines were missed, Damascus had committed to removing its entire stockpile by 27 April, while the overall UN deadline is still 30 June. Ms. Kaag, head of the OPCW-UN mission, acknowledged the removal of a substantial amount of chemical weapons material but highlighted that destruction is still pending, underscoring the urgency of removing the remaining material from the final site to achieve the ultimate deadline.
